evidence: Page 46 (§2.1.2): "[1P][FACT] (Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff.)" and "[1P][DERIVED] (Wan2.2 TI2V-5B configuration, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff.)"
issue: A DERIVED label is attached to a configuration statement (model/card geometry, i.e. what the source states) rather than to an arithmetic result computed from stated inputs. Elsewhere in the book (Preface, p. xvi–xvii; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 Note 1) DERIVED is defined strictly as "computed by arithmetic from stated inputs" and FACT as "directly stated by the source". Page 75 (§3.6.2) labels the same Wan2.2 counts "[1P][FACT]" ("at about 27B total and about 14B active parameters as published"). The same source, same kind of content, therefore carries FACT on p. 75 and DERIVED on p. 46 — an internal contradiction in the evidence taxonomy.
fix_instruction: Change the p. 46 second label from [1P][DERIVED] to [1P][FACT] (the configuration is a source-stated fact, matching §3.6.2's treatment of the same Wan2.2 counts), or reword the sentence so the label applies to an actual arithmetic result.

evidence: Page 33 (§1.3): "If average request is ~9.2K input + ~300 output ≈ 9.5K tokens per request, and traffic is ~10 req/s, then the system ingests: • Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k). • Output tokens/s: 300 ×10 = 3,000 tokens/s output. • Roughly 30× more input tokens than output tokens in this workload (9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, carried book-wide as the canonical ~30×, Ch. 4, Table 4-2)."
issue: The 30× input/output ratio is presented in Ch. 1 as the canonical book-wide constant and is explicitly tied to Ch. 4 Table 4-2, but Table 4-2 (p. 76–79, the canonical-scenario provenance ledger that the book designates as the single authority for canonical values) contains no input/output ratio row — it lists input tokens 9,200 and output tokens 300 separately and never states a 30× ratio. The same chapter-1 text calls Table 1-1 (p. 36) "Token throughput of the canonical workload", but the ratio row in that table is itself labeled "canonical scenario [DERIVED]" with the derivation "9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, rounded down to the canonical ~30× for convenience (not to the nearest integer, 31)". So the ratio's authoritative home (Table 1-1) contradicts the cross-reference Ch. 1 makes to Table 4-2.
fix_instruction: Either add an explicit input/output ratio row to Table 4-2 (Ch. 4, p. 76–79) with its [canonical scenario][DERIVED] status, or correct the Ch. 1 citations from "Ch. 4, Table 4-2" to "Table 1-1" so the ratio's provenance points at the table that actually records it.

evidence: Page 55 (Fig 3.4 caption): "1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)" and "MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on"; the body text above the figure reads "per token: top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB".
issue: The figure's own arithmetic is internally inconsistent: 8 experts × 11.4 GB = 91.2 GB of experts plus the always-on block gives 91 + 3 = 94 GB resident, but the always-on block is stated elsewhere in the same chapter as ~1.4B params (≈2.8 GB at FP16), not 3 GB — and the figure's own body text uses 1.4B/25.6 GB for the active read (11.4 GB + 2.8 GB = 14.2 GB, not 25.6 GB). The caption's later gloss tries to patch this: "The figure's ~23 GB label for the two active experts is their resident weight (2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 GB, rounded to 23 GB); the 25.6 GB per-token read adds the ~2.8 GB of always-on attention/shared weights (1.4B × 2 bytes)" — but 22.8 + 2.8 = 25.6 GB only if the 11.4B figure is 2 × 5.7B experts, which contradicts the figure's stated "top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B". A reader cannot reconcile 2 × 5.7B (=11.4B) + 2.8 GB with a 25.6 GB read without silently recomputing 12.8B × 2 B = 25.6 GB, which is a different decomposition from the one printed.
fix_instruction: Fix the Fig 3.4 panel arithmetic so the always-on block is consistently ~1.4B params ≈ 2.8 GB (not 3 GB), and rewrite the per-token read line so it reads 'per token: 2 experts = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B active → 25.6 GB read (12.8B × 2 B)' rather than splitting 25.6 GB as '23 GB + 2.8 GB' while simultaneously printing 11.4B + 2.8 GB as the component sum.

evidence: Page 96 (sidebar table): "Cloud, 6 hosts — default paid-occupancy input | $87,600 | ≈ $14.04 | 730 h/mo (paid occupancy) | occupancy INPUT, not a measured duty cycle — 730-hour spend over an active-hours volume: an hour-basis mismatch, not a per-request unit cost (quote ≈$3.33/1K instead)".

The table's 6-host row therefore prints a single "Monthly" column ($87,600) whose Per-1K value ($14.04) is explicitly disowned by the qualifier, while the hour-matched row below it prints $20,800 and $3.33 — but no row tells the reader that $87,600 and $20,800 are the same fleet at different hour bases, and the p. 95 narrative presents "~$87.6K–$306.6K/mo at full utilization" as the workload's spend while the per-1K reconciliation on p. 98 names only (c) ~$3.33/1K as the figure to quote. Two mutually exclusive monthly numbers for one fleet are placed in adjacent columns without an in-table pointer to which one the $/1K column is derived from.
fix_instruction: In the p. 96 sidebar table, add an explicit row-level pointer in the 6-host paid-occupancy row's Qualifier column naming the alternative hour-matched figure ($20,800/mo ≈ $3.33/1K) and mark the ≈$14.04 Per-1K cell as 'hour-basis mismatch, not comparable', so the two monthly figures for one fleet are reconciled inside the table rather than only in the p. 98 prose.

evidence: Page 37 (§1.5 Common Mistakes): "• Ignoring the input/output asymmetry. Treating a request as 'one unit' hides that input-heavy workloads tend toward high prefill compute and KV-capacity pressure, while output-heavy ones are decode-dominant (run-time per generated token) — opposite bottlenecks with opposite fixes. (Note: 'capacity pressure' is a memory-capacity constraint, not a memory-bandwidth bound; see Ch. 4/8.)"
issue: The cross-reference "see Ch. 4/8" is not a resolvable reference under the book's own convention. The Preface (p. xix) defines the reference form: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... so § 7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference" and "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." "Ch. 4/8" names two chapters joined by a slash with no section anchor and no target topic — it does not resolve to a specific discussion, and Ch. 4's Chapter-Question scope (workload characterization) does not contain a capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, while Ch. 8 (Compute) and Ch. 7 (Memory) do. The note's own content — that KV pressure is a capacity constraint rather than a bandwidth bound — is stated in Ch. 7 §7.3 (p. 143, the concurrency ceiling) and Ch. 8 (roofline), but Ch. 4 does not carry it as its defining content.
fix_instruction: Replace "see Ch. 4/8" with resolvable anchors that actually state the capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, e.g. "see § 7.3 (concurrency ceiling) and § 8.2 (roofline ridge)", so the reference follows the book's § N.M convention and points at sections that discuss the cited point.

evidence: Page 132 (§6.8): "Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21. That is the capacity floor, which is the max of the named screens, not the prefill compute screen alone: case (i)'s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little's-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds (Ch 8 §3; Ch 17)."
issue: The mini-case's own arithmetic contains a contradiction the text does not flag: it computes the fleet oversubscription as 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H and then, two paragraphs earlier, says the 40 rps peak "demands 40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s ≈ 18.6 host-equivalents" for a single host — but 51.6 ÷ 2.77 = 18.6, so 18.6 is the SINGLE-HOST requirement (H = 1), while the text then reads "the fleet oversubscription at peak is 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H" and concludes "on the single host this mini-case assumes ... that is a ~4.7× oversubscription at baseline and 18.6× at the peak". The prefill screen for the fleet is then given as "⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts", i.e. the single-host-equivalent figure is used as the fleet host count without the reader being told that 18.6 is already a host-equivalent count (18.6 hosts needed), not an oversubscription ratio that must be divided by H again. The ratio and the absolute count are the same number used in two roles (an oversubscription factor at H=1 and a host count at fleet level), which is exactly the unit conflation the chapter elsewhere warns against.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the mini-case's prefill arithmetic to keep the two roles separate: state the peak prefill demand as 51.6 PFLOP/s, the single-host sustained capacity as 2.77 PFLOP/s, the host-equivalent requirement as 51.6 ÷ 2.77 ≈ 18.6 hosts, and the oversubscription at H hosts as 18.6/H — then take the prefill screen as ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts explicitly as a host count (not a factor), and state that the KV-residency screen's 21 hosts is the binding one.
